sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Horsham, PA?
sections.html:
Horsham Township asks every seller of a residential property to complete a township inspection and certification before settlement, so build that step into your timeline from day one. The rest of the sale follows the usual Pennsylvania pattern, with Montgomery County handling assessment, recording and transfer tax.

Horsham sits in Montgomery County about ten miles north of Center City Philadelphia. It covers 17.32 square miles, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 27,882 residents is up 5.0 percent from the April 2020 base. Homes here are worth far more than in older Pennsylvania cities, so a delay of even a few weeks costs real money in carrying costs and interest.

A fast sale to a cash buyer is one route, a listing is another, and a for-sale-by-owner deal is the third. All three need the township certification below, because the rule attaches to the property transfer rather than to the type of buyer.

sections.h2: What is Horsham Township like for homeowners?
sections.html:
It is a suburban home-rule township that grew mostly after World War II. William Penn's surveyors laid out the township's lines, and Horsham was established in 1717. Early settlement clustered around the Friends meeting house at Horsham and Easton Roads, and the township had only about 1,300 people in 1890. The count climbed from 3,663 in 1950 to 8,933 in 1960 and 13,888 in 1970.

Today the township includes the villages of Horsham, Hallowell, Prospectville and Maple Glen. Mail comes through five ZIP codes: 19044 for Horsham, plus parts of the township that use Hatboro, Ambler, Chalfont and North Wales codes. Natural features include Park Creek, Little Neshaminy Creek, Pennypack Creek and Wissahickon Creek.

  • Schools: the Hatboro-Horsham School District, with Keith Valley Middle School and Hatboro-Horsham Senior High School.
  • Parks: about 815 acres of township parkland, a trail network that includes the Power Line Trail, and the 42 acre Graeme Park with its colonial governor's house.
  • Climate: a hot summer humid continental climate, averaging about 32 degrees in January and 77 in July.

The township's biggest recent land story is the former Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base Willow Grove, which closed in 2011 after 68 years. Surplus land from the base is about 8 percent of the township's area and is subject to a redevelopment plan, while the Air National Guard remains on the 200 acre site as Biddle Air National Guard Base.

sections.h2: Which roads and employers shape Horsham home values?
sections.html:
Buyers here shop by commute and by corporate campus. Easton Road (Route 611) runs north to south through the eastern side, Horsham Road (Route 463) crosses the center, and Welsh Road (Route 63), Limekiln Pike (Route 152) and Bethlehem Pike (Route 309) frame the edges. The Willow Grove interchange of the Pennsylvania Turnpike sits just south in Upper Moreland Township.

SEPTA bus Route 55 follows Route 611, and the township runs a weekday rush hour shuttle called h.o.p.s. between the office parks and the Fort Washington station on the Lansdale/Doylestown Regional Rail line. The Census Bureau reports a mean commute of 28.6 minutes for Horsham workers.

Employers named for the township include Janssen Biotech and Janssen Pharmaceuticals, both Johnson & Johnson subsidiaries, plus corporate offices for Bimbo Bakeries USA, Penn Mutual and SofterWare, and a UPS hub.

sections.html:
Horsham is a high value, mostly owner occupied township, and the figures below show how far it sits from the state's older cities.

At a $473,100 median, a one percent state transfer tax alone is more than $4,700 on a typical deed, before any local share. That is why sellers here read the settlement statement closely.

sections.h2: What does Horsham's property transfer certification require?
sections.html:
The township requires an inspection of every residential property before a transfer. The application and fee are submitted to the Horsham Township Municipal Building at 1025 Horsham Road within the 90 days before settlement.

  • A township inspector checks the curb and sidewalk in front of the property.
  • The street address must be posted and easy to see from the road.
  • The seller certifies that working smoke detectors are in the house.

Schedule the inspection early enough to fix a cracked sidewalk slab or a missing house number before settlement. Questions go to the Code Enforcement department at (215) 643-3131.

The township also issues tax certifications through the township tax collector. Send the requester's contact details, the parcel number, the property address, the owner's name and a $30 check per parcel made out to Horsham Township, along with a stamped return envelope if you want it mailed. A title company normally handles this, but a seller handling a sale directly will need to order it.

sections.h2: How do Montgomery County assessments and tax sales touch a Horsham sale?
sections.html:
The county Board of Assessment Appeals sets the values used for county, township and school district taxes, and an annual appeal is due by August 1 to apply to the following tax year. That same August 1 date applies to real estate tax exemption applications. State law requires annual appeals to be decided by October 31 so changes reach the rolls and taxing bodies by November 15.

The board advises mailing deadline filings with a hand-cancelled postmark, a Certificate of Mailing or certified mail, because postal delays can mark a timely envelope late. You can also hand deliver in Norristown on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. The board's phone line is 610-278-3761.

If the house carries unpaid taxes, the county Tax Claim Bureau enters the picture. It holds an upset sale each September and December and a judicial sale at least once a year in August and December. Upset sale buyers take the property subject to its liens, while a judicial sale presents it free and clear. Clear any delinquency before listing so it does not surface at closing.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale the better choice in Horsham?
sections.html:
A cash sale helps most when the property does not fit a conventional buyer's loan, or when the seller cannot wait through showings. Examples are a house with deferred roof or mechanical work, an estate property that needs to close before the next tax bill, or a seller relocating out of the area.

Because Horsham values are high, compare any cash figure with a full net sheet: list price, agent commission, transfer tax, repairs to pass the township inspection, and carrying cost. If you want a cash offer on a Horsham house in its current condition, you can ask Cash Home Buyers for one and compare it against that sheet.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required to sell a house in Horsham Township?
faqs.a: Yes. The township's Residential Property Transfer Certification Program requires an inspection of every residential property before transfer, covering the curb, the sidewalk and the posted address, plus a seller certification of working smoke detectors. Submit it within 90 days before settlement.

faqs.q: How much does a Horsham tax certification cost?
faqs.a: The township's tax collector charges $30 per parcel, paid by check to Horsham Township. Include the parcel number, property address and owner name, and say how you want the certification returned.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a Montgomery County assessment?
faqs.a: August 1 each year for an annual appeal, and it takes effect for the following tax year.
The Hatboro-Horsham School District serves the township, along with neighboring Hatboro. Its schools include Keith Valley Middle School and Hatboro-Horsham Senior High School.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Horsham house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the unpaid amount must be cleared at or before closing. If the taxes go to the county Tax Claim Bureau, the property can end up in an upset or judicial sale, so pay or arrange the balance before that point.
